exemplars.title: Memoro: Using Large Language Models to Realize a Concise Interface for Real-Time Memory Augmentation
exemplars.why: Memoro is the clearest push-versus-pull instance: one memory-assistance capability operates either through explicit voiced queries or queryless predictive assistance, with only the interaction discipline changing.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over SceneScout because its explicit-query versus predictive-assistance contrast maps more directly onto the signature’s canonical pull-query versus push-stream mechanism.

exemplars.title: SceneScout: Towards AI-Driven Access to Street Level Imagery for Blind Users
exemplars.why: SceneScout exposes the same street-level imagery through either predetermined route traversal or free, user-directed exploration, providing unusually concrete alternative navigation disciplines for the same accessibility need.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over the recommendation-explanation study because the abstract specifies both modes’ operational navigation rules more concretely and ties them to a consequential real-world accessibility task.

exemplars.title: Explaining Recommendations through Conversations: Dialog Model and the Effects of Interface Type and Degree of Interactivity
exemplars.why: The study presents recommendation explanations either as a predetermined sequence of graphical steps or through a chatbot-like natural-language interface, with experimental interface assignment acting as the selector.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over PromptMaker because it more clearly establishes two presentation and navigation disciplines for the same explanatory content, whereas PromptMaker’s quote establishes authoring modes but does not show the structured mode’s fields or selection behavior.

notes: The final three follow the consensus order; no score was adjusted by more than 0.3. The evidence is concise rather than exhaustive: Memoro’s abstract does not explicitly prove that both modes surface identical memory content or describe the selector; SceneScout’s abstract does not explicitly state switching behavior; and the recommendation-explanation abstract establishes the compared interfaces but gives neither outcome results nor proof that every explanation item was held identical. These limitations reduce confidence in implementation details, but each quote still demonstrates the required pair of mutually alternative interaction disciplines more directly than the excluded candidates. PromptMaker was the closest exclusion.
